item.title: [New] Exchange Online Change Optics report is GA: it lists onmicrosoft.com external traffic and Direct Send traffic before enforcement
item.description:
Direct Send is a spoofing path that Reject Direct Send closes; the report is the inventory of legitimate senders you need before you switch it on.

Exchange Online · Open the DRS scenario in the Change Optics report, list the legitimate Direct Send senders, move them to a connector or authenticated submission, then enable Reject Direct Send.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 5 days] Canada time-zone change on 1 November: Outlook users in BC, Alberta and Manitoba must switch time zone and recheck meetings; an Exchange Online remediation cmdlet is due 28 October
item.description:
Not a security change, but a time-zone shift moves timestamps that sign-in, audit and detection queries correlate across; Teams Rooms devices one hour behind Windows also misreport meeting times.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-01 · Before 1 November make sure Windows devices in the affected regions have the October 2026 updates, update Edge and WebView2 on Teams Rooms on Windows, and plan to run the Exchange Online remediation cmdlet for non-recurring meetings once Microsoft releases it (target 28 October).

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 5 days] Outlook on the web and new Outlook will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments by default from early November, in every OWA mailbox policy
item.description:
MSIX packages are an established malware delivery format, so this closes an attachment path by default. The cost falls on teams that distribute line-of-business app packages by mail, which will fail without an error anyone anticipated, and the change reaches custom policies too, not only the default one.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-01 · Search mail flow for .msix and .msixbundle attachments over the last 90 days; if a business process depends on them, move it off email rather than adding the types to AllowedFileTypes, and record the decision before early November.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 3 days] Cross-tenant calendar sharing on Cross-Tenant Access Policy slips to 30 October; EWS-based Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing keep breaking as EWS is disabled
item.description:
Partners lose sight of free/busy and shared calendars as EWS reaches the tenant; the usual workaround — re-enabling EWS — keeps a legacy, high-privilege API surface open for another five months.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-10-30 · Run Get-OrganizationRelationship and Get-SharingPolicy as the post shows; migrate Free/Busy and MailTips now and Calendar Sharing after 30 October, and if you set EWSEnabled to True, record it as a time-boxed exception ending 1 April 2027.

item.title: [New] Exchange Online starts turning EWS off: the Exchange team says deprecation begins now, blocked EWS apps can be unblocked only until April 2027
item.description:
Every EWS application still in use, Apple Mail and Calendar on macOS and classic Outlook for Mac among them, either breaks now or survives on a temporary exception that re-opens the protocol Midnight Blizzard used; the exception expires on 1 April 2027 regardless.

Exchange Online · Pull the EWS usage report, list the apps by App ID, decide per app whether it gets a temporary entry in the EWS allowed App IDs list, and alert on any change to EwsEnabled or EwsAllowedAppIDs in the Exchange admin audit log.

item.title: [New] Exchange Online: the Change Optics report, which shows the traffic an upcoming service change would affect, is generally available
item.description:
Mail-flow enforcement changes (connector, authentication and sender rules) break traffic you did not know about; a report of affected traffic before enforcement is the evidence to prepare for that.

Exchange Online · Have the messaging team open the report and check which of your connectors or senders it lists before the next Exchange enforcement date.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Exchange Online: users can send from any of their mailbox's aliases once an admin turns it on (generally available)
item.description:
Once enabled, the From address of outbound mail can be any alias rather than the primary address, so DLP rules, transport rules and hunting queries that match on the primary SMTP address miss mail sent from an alias.

Exchange Online · Before enabling it, review transport and DLP rules and advanced hunting queries on EmailEvents that key on SenderFromAddress for the primary address only, and decide whether aliases should be allowed tenant-wide.
